title: U.S. House · Mississippi's 2nd District
area: The Mississippi Delta and parts of Jackson

context.text: Bennie Thompson defeated Evan Turnage and Pertis Williams III in the March 10, 2026 Democratic primary. Ron Eller defeated Kevin Wilson in the Republican primary.

priorities.text: Has focused on emergency management, citing his role restructuring FEMA after its handling of Hurricanes Katrina and Rita.
Lists health care as a continuing priority for Mississippi.
Has worked on civil rights issues throughout his tenure.

positions.summary: Opposed repealing the Affordable Care Act and highlights the coverage it extended to uninsured residents of Mississippi's 2nd District.
positions.quote: Congressman Thompson cast a vote against a repeal of the Affordable Care Act.

positions.summary: Says he and congressional Democrats are committed to investing in renewable energy and clean-technology research to create jobs and reduce pollution and dependence on foreign oil.
positions.quote: To create the next generation of clean energy jobs, make our nation more secure and reduce the pollution that causes global warming, Congressman Thompson and Congressional Democrats are committed to investing in our nation's clean energy future.

record.text: Chaired the House Committee on Homeland Security during the 117th Congress (2021-2022).
Chaired the House Select Committee to Investigate the January 6th Attack on the United States Capitol.

candidates.name: Ron Eller

priorities.text: Describes himself as a 'blue collar guy' running against career political elites, saying elected officials often lack real-world experience.
priorities.quote: I am blue collar guy and not part of political elite that wishes to divide us the little people so that they can hold the reins leadership over us.

priorities.text: Lists economic development, border security, education, and limited government/taxation among his policy priorities.
Serves as Mississippi chairman for Term Limits, an organization advocating for congressional term limits.

positions.summary: Under a "Right to Life" heading his campaign website says Mississippi's law allowing abortion only to save the mother's life is his preferred approach, and that abortion providers should not receive government funds.
positions.quote: I believe that the Mississippi Law that was upheld by the US Supreme Court, that abortion is to be done only to save the life of the mother, is a commonsense approach to abortion.

positions.summary: His campaign website says the U.S. should not cut its use of fossil fuels and should use all forms of energy.
positions.quote: We can not and should not cut our use of fossil fuels.

statements.quote: Concealed carry licenses should be valid across all jurisdictions like an individual’s driver’s license.
Any state, and/or local government that declares itself a sanctuary should be ineligible to receive any federal funding and aid.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions come from his campaign issues page (also reproduced in his 2026 Ballotpedia survey). The page also covers voter ID and border security; those statements were not mapped to the proof-of-citizenship or deportation issues because they do not address those statements directly.

candidates.name: Bennie Foster

priorities.text: Campaign theme "People Over Politics": says the district is failing because of broken systems and calls for accessibility and accountability from elected leaders.
priorities.quote: People Over Politics. Great success is not a secret, it's a system. Our district is failing because of broken systems.

priorities.text: Campaign theme "Results over Rhetoric": criticizes current leadership for what he calls grandstanding rather than problem-solving.
Says he wants to empower local leaders across the district's 28 counties.

positions.summary: His campaign website says education tax money should follow the student and that parents should have alternatives to the traditional path.
positions.quote: tax money paid by parents towards their child’s education should be well accounted for and follow the student.

positions.summary: His campaign website says he does not support elective abortion, with exceptions to save the mother's life and for miscarriage.
positions.quote: While Foster does not support elective abortion, he does believe exceptions should be allowed in the case of saving the life of the mother, and miscarriage.

statements.quote: Foster also believes we must have accountability for our immigration enforcement officers, and supports requiring body cams, increased training, and better vetting of new ICE agents to ensure no rights are being violated.
statements.context: On his campaign website (written in the third person)

candidates.researchNotes: Positions come from his campaign Policies page (written in the third person) and his Ballotpedia survey. The site also lists Vote411 and Mississippi Free Press questionnaires, which were not retrieved. Foreign-aid language was not mapped to the Israel-aid issue because it does not name Israel.

researchNotes: Basic-tier research. No documented issue positions with direct sourcing found for Bennie Thompson beyond his office's general issue-area pages; no positions found for Bennie Foster beyond his survey priorities. Thompson's federal key votes and FEC finance totals are added separately by script. Biography gaps: Ron Eller and Bennie Foster have no campaign website or news profile found; their biographies rely on Ballotpedia and their Candidate Connection surveys.
